title: Chicken under a brick
summary: Flattened and pressed, the bird cooks in a single plane — thigh and breast finish in the same minute instead of arguing about it.
makeAhead: Dry-brine uncovered on the top shelf, twenty-four hours ahead. This is the whole difference between good skin and shattering skin.

image.alt: Chicken under a brick, charred lemon, herb sauce

title: Cacio e pepe, properly
summary: Four ingredients, and three of them are technique. The sauce is starch, fat and agitation — if it breaks, it broke because the pan was too hot, not because you were short of cheese.

image.alt: Cacio e pepe, pepper-flecked, in a warm bowl

title: Charred cabbage, brown butter
summary: Cut face down, undisturbed, until the flat side is genuinely black at the edges. Cabbage has enough sugar to behave like an onion if you let it.
forkPoint: Before the butter goes in, at step 4 of 6

image.alt: Charred cabbage wedges, blackened cut faces, brown butter

title: White beans, long cooked
summary: Three hours of nothing happening, and then everything has happened. Keep the liquid — it is the reason to make this rather than open a tin.
makeAhead: The whole pot, up to four days ahead. It is better on day two and best on day three.
forkPoint: At step 6 of 9, when the pot divides

image.alt: White beans in their liquid, olive oil, rosemary

title: Green sauce for everything
summary: Chopped, not blended. A blender makes a smoothie and a knife makes a sauce, and the difference is whether you can still see what went into it.
makeAhead: Make it the day before. The parsley darkens and the anchovy stops announcing itself.

image.alt: Coarse green herb sauce, oil separating at the edge

title: Focaccia, cold proof
summary: Twenty minutes of work spread across a day, almost none of it consecutive. The fridge does the part that used to need a schedule.
makeAhead: Mix the dough and put it straight in the fridge. It wants twenty-four hours and will tolerate seventy-two.

image.alt: Dimpled focaccia, olive oil pooling, coarse salt

title: Smashed potatoes
summary: Boiled soft, crushed flat, then roasted hard. Smashing is not a flourish — it is how you turn one surface into nine.
makeAhead: Boil and smash them, then refrigerate on the tray. They roast from cold without complaint.

image.alt: Craggy smashed potatoes, deeply browned edges

title: Pressed pork belly
summary: Braised until it gives, then pressed cold overnight and seared under weight. The pressing is what makes it a slab instead of a pile.
makeAhead: Braise and press up to three days ahead. The sear takes eight minutes from the fridge.

image.alt: Pressed pork belly, lacquered top, sharp square edges

title: Flattened quail, two ways
summary: Small birds, high heat, and a weight — the whole cook is over in nine minutes, which means every one of them counts.

image.alt: Two flattened quail, one glazed, one plain, in a black pan

title: Cabbage, weighted
summary: The same press you use on a bird, on a vegetable. Nothing is being rendered, so it happens in a quarter of the time and the principle is identical.

image.alt: Cabbage steaks pressed flat in a pan under a weight

title: Beans and greens, brothy
summary: What the second half of a pot of beans is for. Looser, greener, and finished in the bowl rather than the pan.
forkPoint: Before the pancetta, at step 2 of 5

image.alt: Brothy beans with wilted greens, oil on the surface

title: Anchovy butter, for everything
summary: Not a recipe so much as a thing to have. It turns bread, fish, steak, and any green vegetable into dinner without being noticed.
makeAhead: Rolled in paper it keeps two weeks in the fridge and three months in the freezer.

image.alt: A roll of anchovy butter, cut into coins
